one_liner: Safe-Rust QOI image codec (crate qoi) that decoded about 1.5x and encoded about 1.3x faster than reference qoi.h.
what_it_does: Encodes and decodes the QOI lossless image format (8-bit RGB or RGBA) in pure safe Rust, with no_std support. The API is Rust-only: encode_to_vec / decode_to_vec one-shot functions, Encoder and Decoder types that work on pre-allocated slices or std::io streams, and Decoder::with_channels to convert between RGB and RGBA on decode. Files are standard QOI and the same size as qoi.h output, but there is no C ABI, so a C++ program would need its own extern "C" shim plus Cargo in the build.
how_it_is_fast: The decoder walks the input with Rust slice patterns (match data { [b1 @ QOI_OP_INDEX..=QOI_OP_INDEX_END, tail @ ..] => ... }), so chunk dispatch and the length checks collapse into one match without per-byte bounds checks, and it is monomorphised over the output channel count (3 or 4) and over whether QOI_OP_RGBA chunks can occur. Runs are written with slice fill, INDEX and RUN chunks skip the colour-index update, and the 6-bit hash (r*3 + g*5 + b*7 + a*11) mod 64 is one 64-bit multiply on the packed pixel. The encoder writes into a pre-sized slice through a small Writer trait, range-tests DIFF and LUMA deltas with OR-mask tricks, and emits QOI_OP_INDEX instead of a length-1 QOI_OP_RUN. Everything is scalar code: there are no SIMD intrinsics and no unsafe blocks.
when_to_use: Rust programs that need very fast lossless 8-bit RGB/RGBA encode and decode and can accept PNG-class or worse compression: asset caches, screenshots, intermediate frames.
no_std or embedded Rust targets (core only, with an optional alloc feature).
Decoding untrusted QOI in Rust where memory safety matters: the crate has #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and the README says it is fuzz-tested and round-trip-tested against qoi.h.
Streaming encode or decode straight from std::io Read/Write without buffering the whole file.
when_not_to_use: C++ projects: there is no C API, so an FFI layer and a Rust toolchain are needed; the reference qoi.h or the catalogued C++ qoixx drop in directly.

Decoding RGBA files to RGB with Decoder::with_channels(Channels::Rgb) when alpha is not all 255: the RGB path hashes pixels with alpha forced to 255 (Pixel<3>::as_rgba(0xff) in the slice decoder, Pixel<3>::hash_index in the stream decoder), so its colour index drifts from the encoder's and later QOI_OP_INDEX chunks return wrong colours. Found by code reading on master and 0.4.1, not covered by any test.

The crates.io release 0.4.1 (2022-10-16, nearly all of the 68.4M downloads) with QOI files from other encoders or on big-endian hosts: it lacks master's 2025 fixes for black pixels decoded as transparent when the first chunk is a run (issue #16, PR #17; it hit image-rs/image and GNOME glycin), the stream decoder's index update on runs, and decode_to_buf with an oversized buffer (#18). Its encoder hash is wrong on big-endian targets and produces malformed images (open issue #26, s390x). A request for a new release (issue #14, April 2025) has no reply.

Interop with files whose header says 3 channels but that contain QOI_OP_RGBA chunks: qoi.h decodes them, qoi-rust (master too) returns an error, and the maintainer noted in PR #17 that upstream's phoboslab/qoi#258 test files stay incompatible because of this channel mismatch.
When file size matters: QOI compresses no better than qoi.h, and the catalogued QOIR, fpnge or Zpng give better ratios at similar speeds.

integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.61 for crates.io 0.4.1; on master Cargo.toml says rust-version 1.67.0 while the README still says 1.62.0
integration.platforms: Any Rust target, std or no_std; scalar code only. The 0.4.1 encoder is broken on big-endian targets (#26); master's from_le_bytes hash fixes it but is unreleased.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; the API is free functions and per-call Encoder/Decoder values over caller-owned buffers with no global state, so separate images can be coded on separate threads (inferred from the source).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same QOI format and file size, and it decodes qoi.h output, but it is a Rust API with no C ABI, and the default encoder's bytes differ from qoi.h unless the 'reference' feature is enabled

gotchas: The default encoder replaces length-1 runs with QOI_OP_INDEX, so its output is valid QOI but not byte-identical to qoi.h; the 'reference' Cargo feature restores identical output, which Cargo.toml says 'may be slower'.

encode_to_vec zero-fills a worst-case buffer of pixels x (channels + 1) + 22 bytes and truncates it without shrinking, so each returned Vec keeps that capacity; call shrink_to_fit if you hold many encoded images.
Images over 400,000,000 pixels are rejected (QOI_PIXELS_MAX), and the decoder only produces 3 or 4 channels.

The README benchmark is from January 2022: commit 3fb2a4d (11 Oct 2023) changed the reference label from phoboslab/qoi@00e34217 to 8d35d93 without changing a single number, so the table was measured against the Dec 2021 qoi.h and the qoi-fast code of that time, not the current submodule or release.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick qoi-rust in Rust code that needs the QOI format with no unsafe code or with no_std; in C or C++ use the reference QOI (phoboslab/qoi) or qoixx, which also beats qoi.h without an FFI layer, and use QOIR or fpnge when you can choose the format and want better compression.
verified_claims_summary: On one Apple M1 laptop (rustc, C compiler and Cargo profile not stated; qoi.h built by the cc crate at opt-level 3), the author's bench/src/main.rs encoded and decoded 2846 images from the QOI benchmark suite (1.32 Gpixels), taking the median of repeated runs per image and summing them: qoi-rust decoded at 427.4 Mp/s against 282.9 for qoi.h and encoded at 290.0 against 225.3 Mp/s (about 1.5x and 1.3x, derived from page data). The numbers date from January 2022 and were measured against qoi.h at phoboslab/qoi@00e34217, not 8d35d93 as the README now says; the 'MB/s' columns are MiB/s.
status_note: Stale but not abandoned (last commit 2025-07-27, PRs open since 2025); dual MIT/Apache-2.0 and about 1,300 lines of safe Rust, but the only release is 0.4.1 from 2022, so either pin a master commit to get the decoder fixes or wait for a release.
